text.p: The Oman stock exchange index rose to a record in the week to Wednesday closing at 297.72 points from 288.21 points the previous week in hectic trade dominated by investment and banking shares.
The Muscat Securities Market said the index was at its highest point since the bourse opened in 1989.
Trading value rose to 26.1 million rials ($69 million) from 24.1 million rials the week earlier, and the number of shares traded rose to 7.8 million from 7.6 million last week.
The exchange said banking and investment sectors accounted for 82 percent of trade, followed by services, industrials and insurance.
Dhofar International Development and Investment was among the most active stocks, with 885,000 shares worth 3.85 million rials changing hands. The stock closed at 4.690 rials from 3.860 rials.
Of the 79 shares traded in the week, 51 rose, 16 dipped and 21 were unchanged.
